summary: Farming involves many important decisions, and choosing the right crops can be challenging when soil conditions and seasonal changes affect plant growth. For farmers who are not familiar with technology, finding reliable agricultural information online can make the process even more difficult. To address this challenge, our team developed FalconXNasa, an interactive website that brings important planting information together in one place. Farmers can explore which crops may grow well in their area by providing details about their location, soil characteristics, and planting season. The platform also includes optional USDA Plant Hardiness Zone and soil test information to help users consider additional growing conditions. Our project is designed to make farming resources more approachable, especially for people with limited digital skills, without excluding experienced farmers. We hope FalconXNasa can simplify crop selection, improve planning, and encourage farmers to make thoughtful decisions that support healthier crops and more sustainable agriculture.
details:
FalconxNasa is a user-friendly crop compatibility planning website designed to help farmers choose suitable crops based on their soil type and planting season. Our project focuses on helping farmers with limited technical experience by providing a simple and easy-to-navigate website. The experience also uses our website to check the crop compatibility as well.

We create this project because different crops require different soil types, temperatures, and growing seasons. Finding the right crop to grow can be time-consuming and might not be successful, which can be quite difficult. And we also target farmers who have limited technical backgrounds or online agriculture tools. Therefore, our goal is to make crop planning easier and more accessible, regardless of a farm's technical experience as well as farming experience.

For our website, we have a feature where the user can enter their location, select a planting season, select their soil type, and choose the crop they want to grow. Users can provide optional information, such as their USDA growing zone, which helps farmers understand which plants could survive during winter. Moreover, the website includes a crop suitability checker that helps farmers understand whether their selected crop is suitable for their soil, and we also have recommendations to support planting decisions.

We develop our website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to create an interactive interface. For our backend system we use Python. We use Visual Studio Code to program our website. As for team collaboration, we use Git and GitHub to help with the front-end and back-end parts of our website.

What makes our project creative is the focus on simplicity and easy navigation. We designed the website with clear instructions, organized sections, and straightforward navigation so that farmers with limited technical backgrounds can use it. Instead of presenting complex agriculture information, our website makes it easy for the user to navigate around the website.

The intended impact of FalconxNasa is to make agricultural information easier to understand and easy to access. We hope our website can help farmers save time, reduce unnecessary trial and error, and make more informed planting decisions. And we aim to encourage sustainable farming practices and help farmers use their land and resources more effectively.
